source.title: Mid-Ulster Mail, 7 June 1958, p. 8 ("Notice of Result of Elections: Cookstown Rural District Council, election of councillors 1958")
source.publisher: Mid-Ulster Mail (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Returning Officer's Notice of Result (Mid-Ulster Mail, 7 June 1958, p. 8, page image read): no candidate is entered for the division; 'Peter Conway' of Tulnacross, Cookstown is entered in column 7, 'Name of retiring Councillor deemed to be re-elected'

note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors, polled Thursday 5 June 1958. There was no contest: nine Unionists and six Nationalists were nominated for the 16 seats, with no nomination for Beaghmore (Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1958, p. 11). All sixteen divisions are recorded from the Returning Officer's Notice of Result, dated 6 June 1958 (Mid-Ulster Mail, 7 June 1958, p. 8): fifteen returned without a poll and Beaghmore's retiring councillor, Peter Conway, deemed re-elected. No labels are printed. Deemed re-elected: no nomination was received (Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1958, p. 11). Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
